_readme: Every feature GATE that is OFF unless something turns it on must appear here.
The list of gates is DERIVED by AST (api/services/feature_flag_index.py) and
never typed; tests/test_feature_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a new one
Why this exists: a gate that defaults off and is set nowhere is
indistinguishable, from outside the repo, from a gate that is off ON PURPOSE.
PATTERN_VISION_ENABLED=0 was a deliberate retirement; twelve others measured
on 2026-08-30 were simply never decided. Nothing could tell them apart.
status: armed  = set on at least one Railway service (its value is the decision)
dark   = deliberately off; note MUST say why
pending= built, no decision yet; note + since MUST be present
This file records INTENT. It cannot see Railway, so it can drift from reality:
run tools/flag_ledger_audit.py to compare it against what is actually set.

BARS_PROXY_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Arms the /api/bars proxy to the origin tier. Gated a second time by BARS_PROXY_PCT, so this flag alone does not decide how much traffic is proxied.

BUZZ_DIGEST_ENABLED.note: ARMED 2026-09-02 (owner). Posts the ticker-buzz board into #main-chat seven times a session: 10:00, 10:30, 11:30, 12:30, 14:00, 16:15, 17:30 ET, mon-fri. Verified live the same day -- 7/7 checkpoints posted. BUZZ_DIGEST_TIMES is deliberately UNSET so the schedule has one authority, discord_buzz_digest.DEFAULT_TIMES. Destination is BUZZ_DIGEST_CHANNEL (bot token), not a webhook. Rollback is this flag alone: unset it and every slot returns {posted: False, reason: 'disarmed'} with no code change. The ingest poller and the /buzz command are NOT gated on this -- they keep running, so turning the posting off never stops counting. A slot the scheduler never fired is caught up within 20 minutes by discord_buzz_digest.catch_up (riding the 60s poll) and, past that window, pages Discord as a critical chart_health_alert. ⚰️ This entry read status=dark, where=(set on no service), "DELIBERATELY OFF -- ships disarmed by design", and named a single 16:10 ET slot -- for a poster that had already put six boards in front of 750 members that day. tools/flag_ledger_audit.py had it under "LEDGER SAYS OFF, BUT IT IS SET" the whole time; the drift was in the intent file, not the detector.

CATALYST_AV_NEWS_ENABLED.note: Off 2026-09-02, and the precondition was CHECKED rather than assumed: CATALYST_AV_NEWS_KEY is set on no service, so _pull_av_news falls through to the shared ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY (which IS set on web). That is the free ~25 calls/day bucket already shared with the earnings-history widget - and this repo's own notes record that quota as already exhausted by the existing news aggregator. CATALYST_ENGINE_ENABLED is set, and the engine bursts every 5 minutes pre-market, so arming this would spend an exhausted budget on every refresh: it buys no sentiment and can starve a feature that works today. The code is wired and ready - set a dedicated or premium CATALYST_AV_NEWS_KEY and THEN arm this. Arming it without one is not a smaller version of the feature, it is failed calls.

COMPASS_HEALTH_EMAIL_ENABLED.note: Off 2026-09-02 by decision: this gates ONLY the scheduler SEND of the weekly operator email. The compute and the status endpoint are ungated and always callable, so the numbers (chat volume, active users, tool-failure rate) are available on demand without it. Off therefore means no weekly email is being sent, NOT no health data. Whether the owner wants a recurring email is theirs to say, and nothing is lost while it is off.

DEEP_CACHE_ENABLED.note: Off 2026-09-02, and superseded in direction. It builds a bars_cache_deep directory on the pod at boot; the architecture has since moved deep history OFF the web pod to a worker origin plus Cloudflare (BARS_HISTORY_ORIGIN_ENABLED / BARS_HISTORY_PROXY_ENABLED, both armed) precisely so the web pod never holds that volume of data. Arming this would push back toward the failure it was moved away from.

EARNINGS_PREWARM_ENABLED.note: Deliberately off since the 2026-05-27 emergency cost pass, re-confirmed 2026-09-02. Railway redeploys wipe the in-memory cache, so the prewarm re-fired for every earnings ticker on every restart - roughly 60K Haiku/Sonnet tokens per redeploy, times several redeploys a day, which was the primary source of baseline daily burn. On-demand modal clicks still work through the synchronous cache-miss fallback, so the feature is not lost. Setting this to 1 restores the burn.

FLOW_PRUNE_ENABLED.note: Deliberately unarmed, re-confirmed 2026-09-02, and it should stay that way absent an explicit decision. There is NO restore path: the R2 backups run at 02:30 ET, AFTER the 20:00 ET prune, so every snapshot is already post-prune, and flow_backup.py has no restore function at all. Unarmed, the nightly job still reports precisely what it WOULD remove, so the information is available without the risk. The first armed run would be the largest delete this table has ever seen.

FLOW_REST_BACKFILL_ENABLED.note: Off 2026-09-02 pending its own dry run. It recovers a WS disconnect window same-day via Massive REST, and is PARTIAL by construction: REST options-trades are per-contract, so only the enumerable Q-pool is recoverable and newly-surfacing contracts still wait for the T+1 flat file - which heals the gap anyway, one day later. The module's own instruction is to run the read-only audit (flow_gap_autofill) BEFORE enabling. Arm it after that audit, not before.

FMP_BULK_ENABLED.note: Off 2026-09-02: an optimization layer only. It pulls whole-market FMP fundamentals so the per-ticker yfinance call and its politeness sleep are skipped for covered symbols, and every miss falls back to that per-ticker path - which is armed and correct. Off costs latency, never correctness. Not armed because the bulk endpoint availability on the current FMP plan is unverified, and an unverified arm here buys a log full of warnings rather than a speedup.

INDICATOR_VISION_ENABLED.note: Armed 2026-09-02 on web: screenshot -> candidate formulas, the third import door beside pasted Pine/thinkScript/PCF. It was the most visible incomplete edge in the product - the builder offers a Screenshot tab unconditionally, so while this was off EVERY member who clicked it got a refusal. (A GRACEFUL one: it points at the Import and Formula tabs, which reach the same engine. An earlier version told a paying member to ask an admin to set this variable, which is why the sentence now lives with the other refusals.) BOUNDED ON BOTH AXES, verified in code rather than taken from the docstring: require_paid gates it (402), INDICATOR_VISION_MAX_PER_HOUR caps one member at 10 screenshots an hour (429), the flag is checked BEFORE the limiter charges so a member cannot spend their allowance discovering the feature is off, the upload is read one byte past MAX_IMAGE_BYTES and refused, and the route STORES NOTHING - a candidate is a suggestion until the member saves it through the ordinary definition door. WORTH KNOWING: spend is ledgered through catalyst cost_guard, the SAME daily USD budget the catalyst engine draws on. A heavy screenshot day therefore eats into catalyst synthesis, and the cap fails safe by disabling synthesis rather than overspending. If that coupling ever bites, the fix is a separate ledger for this door, not a wider cap. Rollback is this variable.

NOTE_SYNC_OBSIDIAN_ENABLED.note:
ARMED 2026-09-04 on service `web` (staged via `railway variables --set --skip-deploys`, activated by a redeploy; verified by /api/health uptime reset and by GET /api/j2/notes/connectors/status reporting obsidian configured=true connectKind='device').

All three arming conditions from the previous note are satisfied, each against a run rather than a passing suite:
  (1) per-note failure isolation -- landed 2026-09-02 (da289747d, per-note SAVEPOINT in import_confirm + engine.py cursor fix). RE-PROVEN LIVE on the arming day: a real vault push of 6 files returned pushed=5 with tooLarge=['Oversized Note.md'] -- the oversized note was isolated and its 5 siblings landed, which is precisely the data-loss shape this condition existed to block.
  (2) THE FORMER SOLE BLOCKER, now satisfied: the plugin is published at https://github.com/unchartedterritory5995-cyber/obsidian-uct-notebook-sync with tagged GitHub Releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1) carrying manifest.json/main.js/styles.css as assets, and ObsidianConnectModal.jsx links members straight to /releases/latest. The community-directory LISTING is still pending review, which is why the modal's copy reads 'or -- while it is awaiting review -- download the latest release': a member can install it today, which is what this condition asked for.
  (3) realistic-size pair -- landed as a committed rail, test_obsidian_ingest.py::test_a_realistically_large_note_syncs_end_to_end_through_the_real_http_sync_route (210,609-char body, 740,540 bytes converted, lands) plus the oversized-isolation half re-proven live in (1).

Proven live end-to-end on the arming day against PRODUCTION, with the real released plugin driving a real vault: connect-code mint -> redeem -> push (5 staged, 1 oversized isolated) -> server sync created=5 in the member's Notebook -> disconnect -> the revoked device token was refused ('Not authenticated', needsReconnect) and could no longer ingest. Test residue was removed afterwards; the connector is left disconnected.

OI_MORNING_ENABLED.note: Armed 2026-09-02 on flow-worker: the weekday 08:00 ET Morning OI card. Held off earlier in the same session on the grounds that arming it PUBLISHES; that was then checked rather than assumed, and the destination is not what the concern supposed. oi_morning._webhook() falls back OI_MORNING_WEBHOOK_URL -> ALPHA_GOLD_EOD_WEBHOOK_URL -> DISCORD_MASSIVE_WEBHOOK_URL -> DISCORD_LIVE_FLOW_WEBHOOK_URL -> DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL, and on flow-worker only the LAST of those is set - the admin/signups channel, not a member channel. So the card lands in front of the owner, which is how it should be judged before it goes anywhere else. Point OI_MORNING_WEBHOOK_URL at a member channel to change that; it is a deliberate second act, not a side effect of this flag. TIMING WAS PART OF THE DECISION: applying it restarts flow-worker, which drops the OPRA WS, and Massive does not replay - a gap is permanent until the T+1 flat file. Done at 22:43 ET on a Wednesday with the session closed, so the restart cost no tape. Rollback is this variable plus a redeploy.

SCAN_LIVE_SWEEP_ENABLED.note: Deliberately unarmed, re-confirmed 2026-09-02, per the live-scan retirement (2026-08-29): that surface was retired while its engine was kept. Worth knowing before touching it: the job is registered UNCONDITIONALLY and the flag is read PER CALL inside live_sweep_job and again inside run_sweep(mode=live), so arming and rolling back are both env-var-only, with no deploy either way. Downstream rendering already assumes scan_hits_live is empty.

SCREEN_BACKTEST_ENABLED.note: Armed 2026-09-02 on web. Decided rather than left pending: the surface was complete and its safety property was verified against real data before the flip, not assumed. Measured read-only over C:/data/bars.db: 30 symbols x 2024-01-01..2026-06-30 returned a closed coverage receipt (18750 bars in window, 18750 answered, 0 not computable) and reported NO EDGE for close > sma(close,50) - 53.7% strategy against a 53.9% baseline - which is the behaviour of a backtester that is not flattering itself. The lookahead refusal fires by name on every screen reading a scalar we hold no history of (rs_rank, market_cap, pe_ttm), including a bar formula ANDed with one. Bounded and gated: require_paid, INLINE_MAX_SYMBOLS=50 above which it queues off the request thread, and a 1.2M-cell ceiling. The auth rail (tests/test_screener_auth_surface.py) SKIPS while the flag is off, so it was run with the flag on before arming: 213 backtest tests pass in both states, 0 skipped when on. Rollback is this variable alone.

STANDING_FLOW_ENABLED.note: Superseded, and setting it would change nothing - confirmed 2026-09-02. On 2026-08-22 the cron was switched, per owner, from run_standing_cron (60-day Open Flow) to run_weekly_cron (a true 5-day week). The scheduler registration and both run_weekly and run_standing accept EITHER this flag or WEEKLY_FLOW_ENABLED, and WEEKLY_FLOW_ENABLED=1 IS set on flow-worker, so the Friday 16:15 ET job is already registered and firing. This flag now survives only as a redundant second arm for a job that is already armed; the 60-day board it was named for is no longer scheduled.

HISTORY_PREWARM_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Sweeps every symbol's sealed D/W/M history through the public Cloudflare domain so Cache Reserve holds it and no first-time user in any region hits the origin cold.

BARS_API_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Selects the dedicated bars-SERVING entrypoint via the railway.json dispatcher, so app/partner deploys can never restart chart serving. This entry read pending until now for a reason that was not about the flag: tools/flag_ledger_audit.py hardcoded a three-service roster (web, worker, flow-worker) while the project has five, so a flag armed only on bars-api was invisible to the audit and was reported as undecided. The roster is now derived from the project.

BARS_HISTORY_ORIGIN_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Lets the worker serve /api/bars-history as a READ-ONLY origin for the deep ~20GB history db, so Cloudflare can cache deep history worldwide without the web pod ever holding or fetching it (the 2026-08-31 OOM class).

BARS_HISTORY_PROXY_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Makes the web pod's /api/bars-history a reverse-proxy to that worker origin; the web pod keeps only shallow history. On a proxy error it falls back to its own local history rather than 5xx-ing.

INSTANT_UNIVERSE_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Widens the boot-only D/W/M warm pass to the whole reference universe. Deliberately kept OUT of the 5-minute refresh loop and the intraday active set, so it cannot cause a 26k-symbol intraday blow-up.

PERMANENT_DAILY_FRESHNESS_ENABLED.note: Part of the edge-deep-history / instant-charts initiative (specs 2026-08-31 onward); recorded 2026-09-02 after a live read. Arms the after-close daily sweep so the web pod's newer-wins merge cold-populates every empty daily and advances every stale one, and a first view of ANY symbol serves from SQLite instead of shedding a warming 503.
